record.original_question: Given a Coxeter system (W,S) and u <= v in W, construct an explicit combinatorial model for the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q), namely a set M(u,v) and statistic s : M(u,v) -> N such that P_{u,v}(q) = sum_{a in M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}, in a genuinely combinatorial rather than merely recursive way.

evidence.quote: So, given a Coxeter system (W,S) and u,v in W, u <= v, one would like to produce (in some explicit combinatorial way) a set M(u,v) and function s : M(u,v) -> N such that P_{u,v}(q) = sum_{a in M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}.
Problem 1.10. Find a combinatorial interpretation for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system with length function ℓ and Bruhat order ≤. For each pair u,v ∈ W with u ≤ v, the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) ∈ ℤ[q] is the unique polynomial of degree at most (ℓ(v)−ℓ(u)−1)/2 (with P_{u,u}=1) determined recursively by the Kazhdan–Lusztig relations on the Hecke algebra of (W,S), or equivalently by the property that the elements C'_v = q^{−ℓ(v)/2} Σ_{u ≤ v} P_{u,v}(q) T_u of the Hecke algebra are invariant under the standard bar involution.

It is known (and conjectured for all Coxeter systems, proved in many cases) that the coefficients of P_{u,v}(q) are nonnegative integers.

Problem. For an arbitrary Coxeter system (W,S) and arbitrary u,v ∈ W with u ≤ v, exhibit an explicit combinatorial model for P_{u,v}(q): that is, construct a finite set M(u,v) and a statistic s : M(u,v) → ℕ, defined directly from the combinatorial data of the pair (u,v) (for example from the Bruhat interval [u,v] or from reduced expressions for u and v), such that
    P_{u,v}(q) = Σ_{a ∈ M(u,v)} q^{s(a)}.
The construction is required to be genuinely combinatorial — not merely a restatement of the defining recursion — so that the nonnegativity of coefficients of P_{u,v}(q) is manifest from the model.
artifact.status_search_result: Finding an explicit, non-recursive combinatorial interpretation of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials in general Coxeter systems is a long-standing open problem, dating back to Kazhdan and Lusztig (1979). Partial results are known: combinatorial formulas exist for special classes (e.g., 321-hexagon-avoiding permutations, smooth Schubert varieties, certain matroid analogues such as braid matroids), and recent work (2021–2025) has used Bruhat-graph "hypercube decompositions" to attack the related combinatorial invariance conjecture for symmetric groups. However, no general combinatorial model M(u,v) with statistic s is currently known, even for symmetric groups.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: No combinatorial interpretation is known, in general, for the coefficients of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: A general combinatorial interpretation is not known.

status_evidence.title: Towards combinatorial invariance for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: New formula for KL polynomials of symmetric groups based on the Bruhat graph, suggesting an approach to combinatorial invariance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on related combinatorial invariance, but no full combinatorial model in general.

status_evidence.title: Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials: History, Problems, and Combinatorial Interpretations (Brenti)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing finding a combinatorial interpretation of P_{u,v}(q) as a central open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Survey confirms the problem is open.
